metadata.title: Coprime paths: the nine-edge threshold, linear bounds, and reproducible evidence

metadata.description:
This evidence archive establishes the exact nine-edge coprime path threshold P_cop(9) = 17: every two-coloring of the edges of the coprime graph on 1,...,17 contains a monochromatic simple path with nine edges, while a checked coloring at 16 avoids one. The upper bound combines a written extremal classification with independently checked finite host lemmas.

Supporting results independently recertify the earlier reported values P_cop(7) = P_cop(8) = 13 and establish linear bounds with lower limiting ratio at least 2 and upper limiting ratio at most 197*pi^2/595. Earlier values are credited as prior results. The infinite odd-path formula remains unresolved.

The deterministic packet contains 79 pinned source files: proofs, finite certificates, checkers, tests, dependency pins, the author-edited manuscript, literature notes, clearly separated auxiliary explorations, licenses, and per-file hashes. Its metadata and packaging commit is afb384ee910a6f25cadaeabb9cf8a74729a02666. The journal style file is omitted; all listed mathematical checks are self-contained, while rebuilding the journal-formatted manuscript requires the journal template separately.

Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance and separate AI review are disclosed. The complete deduction is a written proof, not formal verification. No new nine-edge UNSAT certificate, human peer review, journal acceptance, established novelty, or legal priority is claimed. Tests and certificate replay verify finite evidence rather than every written argument.

Alexander Richard Towell is the author. Prior constructions, Du, Xi, Deng and Ma, and the graph-theoretic sources used in the proof are credited in the manuscript and record. The main proof was publicly disclosed in project PR9 on October 18, 2026; the revised manuscript and organized evidence became public in PR11 on October 20. These dates are distinct from archival publication. Original prose is CC BY 4.0 and original code is MIT; see the per-file licenses.
